title: Generative Echo Chamber? Effects of LLM-Powered Search Systems on Diverse Information Seeking

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating users' information-seeking behaviors by measuring the proportion of attitude-consistent (confirmatory) queries issued, confirmatory arguments included in written essays, and self-reported post-task opinion polarization (including attitude change, agreement, and trust toward consonant versus dissonant articles) after using conventional web search versus LLM-powered conversational search.

Manipulating the LLM's responses and retrieved documents to exhibit a specific stance (consonant, neutral, or dissonant) relative to the user's pre-existing attitude on controversial political topics (e.g., universal healthcare, sanctuary cities, student loan debt) to test its effect on the user's echo chamber and information-seeking behavior.
